answer: Cross-chain identity binding at the plume: one wallet stakes on two chains, and only the overlap counts as one identity. A reef of duplicate addresses collapses because the binding check reconciles both ledgers before rewards. The yarrow rule is simple—fork your identity and lose both stakes. Cost scales linearly per real user, so farming N identities costs N deposits, never less. It works because duplication is provably expensive, not merely discouraged.
